duration.description: A duration — "90s", "10m", "1h30m" — or a bare number of seconds.

envMap.description: Environment variables, as NAME: value pairs.

workflowRef.description: Another sub-workspace's workflow: "<member>" for its workflow of this same name, or "<member>:<workflow>" for one specific workflow.

cache.description: What a build reads, what it writes, and whether to reuse the result. Declared at the workspace, workflow, or step level; the most specific one wins.

enabled.description: Whether caching is on. Absent means "inherit" — a step that lists inputs without mentioning enabled is saying "these are my files", not "turn caching off".

inputs.description: Glob patterns for the files this build reads, relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT — not to the sub-workspace this section is written in. A build that reads something not listed here will be handed a stale result.

outputs.description: Glob patterns for the files this build writes, relative to the workspace root like `inputs`. These are what gets stored and restored on a cache hit.

env.description: Environment variables that are part of the cache key. A build whose result depends on PROFILE must say so, or switching profiles will silently reuse the other one's artifacts.

exclude.description: Glob patterns never treated as inputs, even when `inputs` would match them, relative to the workspace root like `inputs`. Build output living under a source tree is the usual case.

remoteCache.description: The shared cache this workspace reads from and writes to. Local-only caching needs none of this.

url.description: Base URL of the remote cache server (`ciabatta remote-cache start`).

name.description: The name this project is known by on the server. Defaults to the workspace's own name.

project.description: The identifier the server assigned when this project first registered. Commit it — it is what makes every checkout and every CI runner resolve to the same project.

read_only.description: Read from the remote cache but never write to it. What CI wants for pull-request builds.

tls_verify.description: Verify the server's TLS certificate. Keep it on for anything reachable beyond your own machine.

enabled.description: Turn the remote off without deleting its settings.

fixOption.description: One fix choice offered by a recovery node.

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the UI.

script.description: A bash script to run as the fix, relative to the project root.

run.description: An inline shell command, as an alternative to `script`.

default.description: Run this option automatically in non-interactive mode (plain / CI), where no operator is present to choose. The first `default` option wins.

step.description: A node in the run graph: a normal step, or a recovery node (`recover: true`) entered only via some step's `on_error`.

name.description: Unique node name; the target of `needs` / `on_error` / `retry` edges.

script.description: A bash script to run, path relative to the step's working directory. An alternative to `run`.

description.description: One line on what this step does, and what it expects to be true first. `ciabatta list` prints it, so nobody has to open the file to find out.

owner.description: Who owns this step — a name, handle, or team.

tags.description: Free-form labels — `fast`, `slow`, `integration`. These are what `--filter tag:fast` selects on.

requires.description: Executables that must be on PATH for this step to work. Checked before the graph starts, with the install command from the matching `toolchain:` entry.

timeout.description: Wall-clock limit for this step. When it expires the step is killed and marked timed out, and the rest of the graph carries on.

retries.description: Extra attempts to make when the step fails, for transient errors. Default 0: one attempt, no retry.

persistent.description: A step that never exits on its own — a dev server, a log tailer, a watcher. Its dependents are released immediately and it runs alongside the rest of the graph rather than hanging it. It OUTLIVES the run: the daemon takes ownership as a watch session, so `ciabatta dev` leaves you a server to work against. Stop it with `ciabatta watch --stop <id>`. For a process that exists only to get this run through and should go away with it, use the workflow's `background:` array instead.

continue_on_error.description: Don't fail the whole run when this step fails: its dependents are skipped, every other branch carries on, and the failure is reported at the end. Always applied when a `timeout` expires.

kind.description: The phase this step belongs to. Free-form and cosmetic (it labels the node on the graph) except for `push` and `pull`, which select the built-in registry action.

registry.description: The `registries:` entry a `push` / `pull` step transfers through.

artifact.description: The local file or directory to publish (or where a pull writes to), relative to the step's working directory. A directory is uploaded file by file, preserving its structure.

local_image.description: Docker/ECR only: a local image reference (`name` or `name:tag`) to push. It is retagged to the registry's target reference before pushing.

publish_path.description: Destination path in the registry, with {CIABATTA_*} substitution — or a list of local globs, each uploaded under {CIABATTA_PATH} keeping its relative path.

strip_prefix.description: For the glob-list form of `publish_path`: a leading path fragment stripped from each matched file before it is joined under {CIABATTA_PATH}.

from.description: For a `kind: pull` step: the push step it mirrors, as `<workflow>:<step>` or a bare `<step>` in this workflow. Its transfer fields are copied in, so push and pull can't drift apart.

cwd.description: Working directory for this step's action, relative to the project root. Workflow graphs default it to the owning sub-workspace's directory.

env.description: Environment variables for this step alone, layered over the run's own.

needs.description: Names of steps in this same file that must succeed before this one runs. Cross-workspace dependencies belong on the workflow's `needs:`, not here.

on_error.description: On failure, jump to this recovery node instead of aborting the run.

when.description: Condition(s) that must ALL hold for this step to run. Forms: `VAR == value`, `VAR != value`, `VAR` (truthy), `!VAR`. The variable may carry an `env.` prefix.

skip_if.description: Condition(s) that skip this step when ANY holds — the inverse of `when`.

recover.description: Marks this node as a recovery node: it presents `options` rather than running an action of its own.

message.description: Prompt shown when a recovery node is reached.

retry.description: After a chosen fix succeeds, re-run this node — typically the step that failed.

options.description: The fix choices offered by a recovery node.

cache.description: Cache settings for this step alone, overriding the workflow's and the workspace's. Most steps inherit and never write this.

workspace.description: Which sub-workspace this step came from. Filled in when the graph is compiled — you don't normally write this.

env_files.description: The .env files this step resolves through, outermost first. Set by the workflow compiler — you don't normally write this.
